masterPrompt: Create a photorealistic garage organization BEFORE/AFTER DIPTYCH: exactly TWO equal-width panels filling the canvas, BEFORE on the left, AFTER on the right, vertical seam at exactly 50 percent, no gutter, border, labels, words, logo or watermark. Show the EXACT SAME ordinary American residential garage in both panels from an IDENTICAL locked tripod at the open entrance, 25-28mm lens equivalent, eye height 1.55m. Match geometry, doors, windows, ceiling tracks, fixtures, floor joints, cracks, wall marks, camera perspective, light direction, exposure and shadows. Transform only clutter, removal, cleaning and practical storage. Do not repaint, change windows, widen the room, add epoxy, erase permanent concrete damage or simulate architectural renovation. Retain distinctive useful possessions in recognizable places in the after image. Use achievable black or gray freestanding steel shelves, sensible bins and physically supported hooks. Realistic shelf spacing and loads, grounded objects, coherent tools and bicycles. Preserve access to doors, panels and equipment. Natural documentary smartphone photograph, real material texture and minor imperfections, no CGI gloss, no people, identifiable addresses, plates or private documents. This is an illustrative design concept, NOT documentary proof of a completed job. Apply this scene-specific brief:

scenes.title: Room for the family car
scenes.brief: Two-car garage, off-white walls, back-right six-panel door and two steps, small left-wall window, diagonal concrete hairline crack. Before: cartons, mixed totes, stroller, folding chairs and sports gear across floor. After: same useful items sorted on black shelves at left and rear, black totes with yellow lids, folded stroller reachable and broad clear center.

scenes.title: Small garage, useful space
scenes.brief: Narrow townhouse single-car garage, rear window left of center and rear-right door. Before: moving boxes, plastic tubs, rolled rug and old small bookcase blocking access. After: bulky unwanted bookcase and spare cartons removed, two slim gray shelving units at left, folded ladder on right wall, realistic compact-car clearance.

scenes.title: A place for every bike
scenes.brief: Two adult bikes, teal and black, and two child bikes, red and blue, tangled across a two-car garage floor. After: same four bikes correctly spaced on supported wall hooks, helmets and sports equipment within reach. Each bicycle must have exactly two coherent wheels, believable forks, chain, pedals and mounting contact.

scenes.title: Bring the workbench back
scenes.brief: Unfinished taped drywall, back-right white door, left rectangular window, stained concrete. Existing wooden workbench back-left is buried under tools and cardboard. After: same bench and wood grain, clear top, modest black pegboard above, supported tool hooks, small drawers below, organized lumber and cords; no new room finishes.

scenes.title: Find the holiday boxes
scenes.brief: Ordinary cream-walled garage. Red and green holiday tubs, wreath box, artificial-tree bag, cooler and patio chairs clutter floor. After: same identifiable tubs sorted on steel shelving, tree bag low, folded chairs neatly supported, cooler reachable and clear center.

scenes.title: Ready for the next trip
scenes.brief: Blue cooler, rolled tent, sleeping bags, backpacks, camp chairs, boots and garden cart scattered in a two-car garage. After: same blue cooler on accessible shelf, tent and bags dry in bins, backpacks on wall hooks, boots low, chairs vertical, cart at right wall, parking floor clear.

scenes.title: The garden gear, sorted
scenes.brief: Detached garage with unchanged timber ceiling and concrete. Rakes, shovels, hose, empty plant pots, push mower and gloves scattered. After: same long tools on secure hooks, coiled hose, pots nested, gloves in small bin and mower parked out of central path. No fuel handling, chemical decanting or building alterations.

scenes.title: Remove what no longer belongs
scenes.brief: Simple two-car garage with old worn sofa, damaged flat-pack cabinet, empty packaging and a useful red toolbox. After: unwanted sofa, damaged cabinet and packaging removed; same red toolbox and useful household bins retained at walls. Keep permanent slab marks and original walls unchanged.

scenes.title: Unpack the garage
scenes.brief: Newly occupied standard garage, unpainted drywall seams and ordinary slab. Moving cartons obscure usable plastic shelving. After: useful contents consolidated in storage tubs on the SAME plastic shelves, empty cartons removed, folding table stored flat. No magically added cabinetry or repaired wall finish.

scenes.title: Keep the things that matter
scenes.brief: Older modest garage with family keepsake tubs, spare chairs, empty suitcases and unused household furniture. After: retain distinct blue keepsake tubs and two good suitcases on reachable shelves, remove redundant furniture, clear walking space. No readable personal papers or inferred customer story.

scenes.title: Practice-day storage
scenes.brief: Two-car garage cluttered by soccer balls, basketball, baseball gear, helmets and folding sports chairs. After: same equipment in a freestanding ball basket, modest open shelves, accessible hooks and bins; clear center. Ball shapes and rack supports must be physically consistent.

scenes.title: Winter gear without the pile
scenes.brief: Garage with two pairs of skis, a blue snowboard, boots, poles, snow shovel and plastic sled on floor. After: exact same recognizable gear organized on supported wall rack with reachable boot shelf, shovel hook and sled vertical. Keep original window, entry steps and concrete joints identical.

scenes.title: Make space to move
scenes.brief: Existing modest exercise corner with a folded bench, dumbbells, rolled mat and storage boxes. After: same workout items neatly on low racks and wall hooks, clear usable floor, clutter consolidated on existing shelf. No fabricated new gym equipment, mirrors, floor coating or expensive remodeling.

scenes.title: Tools off the floor
scenes.brief: Small single-car garage, old narrow bench and loose hammers, hand saw, drills and extension leads. After: same bench, simple pegboard with coherent securely hung tools, cords coiled, drills on shelf and central walkway clear. Realistic ordinary DIY organization.

scenes.title: Seasonal storage with a plan
scenes.brief: Two-car garage with empty lightweight luggage and seasonal plastic bins stacked precariously on floor. After: stable freestanding steel shelving with heavier items low and light luggage above shoulder level. No ceiling-mounted loads, no obscured garage door travel or invented supports.

scenes.title: A clear route to the door
scenes.brief: Garage with an existing rear utility closet door and side house entry partly blocked by boxes. After: clear routes to both doors and visible access to equipment, shelving on opposite wall with possessions retained. Do not alter equipment, cover vents, specify code compliance or invent electrical work.

scenes.title: Work with what you own
scenes.brief: Three mismatched usable plastic and metal shelving units scattered among bins and cartons. After: the very SAME three shelves aligned along walls and contents sensibly sorted, cardboard waste removed, floor swept. No purchased replacement shelves, no change in architecture or room size.

scenes.title: A path through a long garage
scenes.brief: Long narrow tandem garage with a small rear window and repeating concrete expansion joints. Before: boxes, garden tools and spare chairs scattered along depth. After: slim storage on one side, chairs folded, tools supported, continuous clear center aisle. Identical depth, width, camera and rear-window size.

scenes.title: Give the extra bay a purpose
scenes.brief: One storage bay of a three-car garage, fixed framing includes edge of partition post at left and rear door at right. Before: assorted cartons, camping tubs and unused side table. After: table removed, camping tubs on back wall shelves, clear bay floor. Do not expand the room or alter the post.

scenes.title: A fresh start, without a remodel
scenes.brief: Older detached garage with aged exposed timber, fixed small window and worn concrete. Before: household clutter, broken cardboard boxes and useful lawn tools. After: practical freestanding shelves and hooks, clutter removed and swept floor. Crucially retain old walls, timber, discoloration and original concrete wear.

scenes.title: An easier way into the house
scenes.brief: Garage entry with two original concrete steps, white door, shoes, backpacks, folding stroller and bags underfoot. After: small freestanding shoe rack, supported bag hooks, stroller folded beside wall, steps and route clear. No new built-in mudroom, remodeled steps or different door.

scenes.title: Make your hobby easy to reach
scenes.brief: Existing folding hobby table with craft boxes, model supplies and small hand tools spread through garage. After: same table clear, small transparent bins on sturdy shelves and useful materials sorted, excess packaging removed. No recognizable logos, readable labels or invented finished workshop.

scenes.title: Bring the parking space back
scenes.brief: Two-car garage with sports equipment, flat-packed boxes, garden tools and unused plastic furniture blocking parking footprint. After: approved-looking unwanted clutter removed, useful equipment stored along perimeter, broad open bare concrete floor. Do not add a car; room, rails and lighting identical.

scenes.title: A place for the everyday things
scenes.brief: Large but ordinary two-car garage, plain drywall, rear-left workbench, back-right entry, small side window. Before: bikes, useful bins, tools and camping equipment mixed on floor. After: practical black steel shelves on both walls, black/yellow bins, properly hung bikes, same usable workbench visible, uncluttered center. Attainable organization only, no luxury remodeling.
